name: Mindaugas Sinkevičius
role: Prime Minister of the Republic of Lithuania (Lietuvos Respublikos Ministras Pirmininkas)
party: Lietuvos socialdemokratų partija (LSDP) — Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats (S&D) in the European Parliament
bio: Mindaugas Sinkevičius, born in Jonava in 1984, a graduate in management (Vilnius University, ISM University of Management and Economics) and law (Mykolas Romeris University) who defended a doctorate at ISM in 2015, has been Prime Minister of Lithuania since 14 July 2026, at the head of the 21st government, the third formed since the Social Democrats won the 2024 Seimas election. A member of the Lithuanian Social Democratic Party (LSDP) since 2004 and its deputy chair from 2015, he was mayor of Jonava District for most of 2011–2026, Minister of the Economy in Saulius Skvernelis's government from December 2016 to November 2017 and president of the Association of Local Authorities in Lithuania from 2019; he became acting party chair when Gintautas Paluckas resigned in July 2025 and was elected chair on 1 May 2026. In 2024 the Kaunas Regional Court and the Court of Appeal convicted him in the municipal 'čekiukai' (expense receipts) case, which cost him the mayoralty, but on 5 March 2025 the Supreme Court quashed the convictions and discontinued the case, finding that his conduct did not entail criminal liability, and he returned as mayor. After the LSDP removed Dawn of Nemunas from the coalition in June 2026, the Seimas approved his appointment on 30 June (80 votes to 2, with 28 abstentions); his coalition with the Union of Democrats 'For Lithuania' and the Farmers, Greens and Christian Families Union holds 75 of the 141 seats. As of October 2026 his government has submitted a 2027 budget that keeps defence spending at 5% of GDP with a projected deficit of 3.8% of GDP, a family package and an average pension rise of about 10%, while he faces questions over his land transactions, his past job at the road builder Fegda, plagiarism allegations about his doctoral thesis (under review by ISM) and a Constitutional Court case on the way his government's programme was submitted.
